# Client content direction, received via WhatsApp on 2026-08-18

Source: Pooja Punjabi (founder, Potbelly Audio), sent as a single WhatsApp message while travelling.
Her closing notes: a floating WhatsApp button across the website "should be good"; she wants our
thoughts; "the content needs refinement, which I'm sure your team would be able to do it"; her trip
ends 2026-08-19 and she can work on it a little after that.

**This file is the content spine. Do not edit it. Refinements go into the build, never back into
this file, so every later pass can diff against what she actually asked for.**

**Two transcription changes, made once, on the way in.** Her original WhatsApp message used em dashes
in five places (Translation & Localisation, International Content Owners, the new-market band, Quality
Control, and We Get the Original) and middot separators in the language list and the referral segment
list. Both were converted to commas here, because the house standard forbids em and en dashes and the
site would have to make that change anyway. Nothing else was altered: no word was added, removed or
reordered. This matters because a later pass reading only this file would otherwise conclude her draft
never contained an em dash.

## What the shape of this document tells us (read before writing a line of code)

1. **She wrote a scroll, not a sitemap.** Eleven sections in reading order, each ending in a CTA.
   There is no page tree, no "Learn more", no service detail page. The default answer to
   "which page does this go on" is: the home page, in her order.
2. **Every CTA is a conversation opener.** Discuss Your Project, WhatsApp Us, Get a Quote, Ask Us,
   Talk to Pooja, Make an Introduction, Listen to Our Work. Zero informational CTAs. The site's job
   is to start a chat, not to educate.
3. **Capability breadth plus one workflow is the pitch.** Nine capabilities, "handled under one
   roof", "One team. One workflow." She is selling the absence of vendor juggling.
4. **Audience-led, not service-led.** WHO WE WORK WITH is nearly as long as WHAT WE DO. Buyers are
   meant to self-identify. That section is a qualifier, not filler.
5. **India first, international as reach.** Eleven named languages, all Indian plus English.
   International shows up as markets content travels to and from. There is no Japan, no Korea,
   no anime positioning anywhere in her brief.
6. **Proof is by ear.** "Hear the difference." "Our work speaks for itself." She explicitly reserves
   space for players. The work section is the centre of the page, not a portfolio afterthought.
7. **Referral is a first-class section.** Unusual on a services site, and it says her pipeline is
   relationship-led. It stays.
8. **Voice: short declarative sentences, no adjective stacking, quietly confident.** "Sounds Good."
   is the sign-off. "Because small mistakes don't stay small in finished content" is the register to
   match. Any copy that reads like an agency brochure is off-brief.
9. **She spells it "Localisation".** British and Indian English throughout. Match her.
10. **Her draft contains em dashes.** House standard forbids them. The refinement pass converts them
    to commas, colons or parentheses. That is a house rule, not a change of meaning.
